Have you been keeping up with the proposed Canal of Nicaragua? I can't remember what the latest was on whether or not the Chinese would go through with this project. I think it started a couple years ago. Would Ometepe Island get caught up in the dredging?

The chinese own the land rights across the country to build it, but the developer went nearly bankrupt about 6 months ago. Then the main Chinese port exploded and made Chinese exports slow way down. The canal dredge were planned to travel within 2 miles of Ometepe Island. They laid a bunch of communications and power cables across the lake, but it is on hold right now. If it continues it will probably be an oil pipe line instead of a canal and hopefully not cross the actual lake, but skirt the Costa Rican border instead or go north through Managua. The Chinese and Indians really want to get cheap Venezuelan oil without the hassle and expense of Panama tariffs. An oil pipeline is a better fit and would not compete with US trade interests in Panama and Costa Rica. It would also be a boon to US oil producers.

Having crossed the Panama Canal four times now (fifth one coming up in a couple months) I was really frustrated when I heard about the plans for Nicaragua. A lot of the articles highlighting the project really made me sad about the impact it would have to the environment in that region. However, I didn't realize the Chinese actually held the land, I thought they were just investing locally in order to drive an outcome to a project they felt would be beneficial. What are they going to do with all the com/power cables now that the canal project is on hold? It'll be interesting to see how that continues to evolve down there.

Can you actually visit Ometepe Island?

Yes, you can visit. I went last August. There's two ferries a day to the Island and they are run by the Nicaraguan government. There are quite a few resort hotels on the island as well as a few hostels. I highly recommend the place. If you go, I recommend hiking all the way up to Madera lake and waterfall. Conception is the active volcano and you might even be able to get a guide to take you to it too. The place also has an amazing butterfly sanctuary, natural history museum, and the lake is comfortable 85º all the time. After you leave the island and head south past Rivas towards Costa Rica, I recommend you check out San Juan Del Sur and the amazing surfing and sea turtle beaches in the area. There is even a cruise ship that stops there a couple times a week.
